messages:
inc-bot: :rotating_light: DETECTED unusual error pattern on serving-runtime pool gpu-rt-7 — high rate of container crashes with CUDA "illegal memory access" and misaligned-address traces. auto-escalation to #incidents.

inc-bot: Summary: 2026-03-15T03:12Z - spike in OOM/ILLEGAL_MEM on 6 pods across 2 nodes (gpu-rt-7, gpu-rt-9). Error loop during model reloads after rolling update.

sahil: I'm on it — taking initial triage. quick check: any customers actively seeing 5xx? @lisa can you surface any CS alerts?

lisa: Customer CS: two customers reported elevated errors for text-generation endpoints (~12% errors in last 5m). No SEC or data exfil reported. I've opened support tickets and pinged affected accounts.

maya: grabbing logs from the crashing containers. seeing repeated stack: 

```
RuntimeError: CUDA illegal memory access
  at serving/runtime/kv_cache.cu:line 214
Backtrace:
  gpu-kernel: pagewalk_deviceaddr()+0x1a3
  runtime: apply_kv_cache()+0x2f
  container: reload_model()+0x5b
```

Also kernel message from node: 

```
[  102.123456] NVRM: GPU at 0000:3b:00.0: an illegal memory access was encountered
[  102.123457] RT: page_walk: misaligned address 0x7ffeffff
```

maya: Notable: crashes cluster around model reloads and attempts to restore large KV caches. Sequence length spiked on those requests.

julian: Can we cordon and drain the two affected nodes to stop churn? I'll prepare replacements and hold rolling update.

sahil: Cordon+drain in progress for gpu-rt-7. Command: `kubectl cordon gpu-rt-7 && kubectl drain gpu-rt-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30`

ops-bot: Drain started for gpu-rt-7; 3 pods evicted. New pods scheduled on gpu-rt-11,gpu-rt-12.

maya: Attempted a restart on one crashed container with `--disable-kv-restore` flag (to skip KV restore) — container stayed up for 7m then crashed again with similar trace. So KV restore likely triggers large pagewalks and kernel path.

julian: Hypothesis: concurrent pagewalks + KV restore cause misaligned device addresses on current kernel/driver combo. Need to test a rollback to older driver or disable parallel KV restore while we triage.

sahil: Agreed. Rolling update paused. I'm initiating a temporary rollout with KV restore disabled for the new model version (canary 10%). Also adding traffic split to fallback model variant (smaller KV) at 20% to reduce pressure.

infra-bot: Provisioning 2 additional GPU warm nodes (gpu-rt-13,gpu-rt-14) for capacity; ETA ~4m.

maya: Capturing coredumps now; uploading to s3://redwood-incidents/4311112222/ for postmortem. Command used: `gdb --batch -ex "set pagination off" -ex "thread apply all bt" -ex quit core /usr/bin/serving`

julian: I'll open a lightweight regression test: recreate a KV restore with varying concurrency on a test node (kernel v5.15 + nvidia-driver 545.34). Need to see repro window.

sahil: Customer impact update: errors dropped from 12% -> 4% after draining nodes and traffic split. still degrading for ~5 customers behind edge caches. @lisa keep CS updated and offer retries/temporary quota bump if they ask.

lisa: Noted. I've messaged affected customers with guidance: temporary fallback endpoint + retries. No escalations yet.

maya: One interesting find — the stack traces show misaligned accesses in `pagewalk_deviceaddr` at offsets that suggest page table entries being torn during concurrent updates. Could be a kernel bug or DMA ordering issue in the driver.

sahil: Will escalate to vendor if we repro. For now the mitigation plan: 1) pause rolling updates, 2) disable KV restore concurrency (serial restore), 3) drain affected nodes, 4) enable fallbacks and traffic split, 5) collect traces and coredumps, 6) schedule oncall handoff.

julian: I'll pick up the overnight oncall. @sahil can you hand off progress and commands executed?

sahil: Handoff -> julian. Actions done: cordoned gpu-rt-7, drained gpu-rt-7, paused rollout, enabled 10% canary variant, traffic split 20% to small-KV fallback, coredumps uploaded, new nodes provisioned. Monitoring: CPU/GPU memory flattening, error-rate trending down. Command history in ops-runbook: /runbooks/incident-4311112222.md (internal).

julian: Thanks. I'll continue monitoring metrics, run the regression repro on the testfarm, and start vendor escalation if we see reoccurrence after reintroducing KV restore. If error rate climbs above 8% again, I'll trigger P1 channel and customer-notify template.

sahil: FYI — I'm leaving the pager; reachable on phone. :thumbsup:

lisa: I'll keep customers updated and set expectation for a detailed postmortem once root cause known.

maya: One more note — heap snapshots show large pinned host buffers during restore; will dump vmmap and kernel dmesg next.

julian: Received. I'll also add a temporary guard in the runtime to reject KV restores when free GPU memory < 30% to avoid immediate repeat while we root-cause. Quick patch incoming to canary.

ops-bot: New canary deployment (kv-guard-enabled) rolled out to 10% traffic.

julian: Monitoring logs and kernel ringbuffer on new canary nodes. If stable for 30m, we can reintroduce controlled restores.

inc-bot: Incident thread created and tagged: severity=high, owners=[maya,sahil,julian].

customer-success-bot: Tickets created for affected customers: CS-2241, CS-2242. Status: notified, workaround offered.

julian: Handing off to night shift. I'll keep the channel open for any regressions. Final note: collect full kernel oops logs and attach to the vendor report — looks like a rare pagewalk ordering issue.

sahil: Copy. Good job everyone. :raised_hands:
